item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Oct 20, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Oct 22, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Ephrata Shadows — Fri Oct 23 — Downtown Ephrata

Join Mainspring of Ephrata, and the Historical Society of the Cocalico Valley, for Ephrata Shadows – a guided historical ghost tour through our downtown streets, where cloaked guides share spine-tingling tales of local legends, unexplained phenomena, and the restless spirits said to still roam the area. Along the way, your guides will share the historical facts about our buildings and the stories behind the folklore. It’s a walking tour for ages 16 and up that blends real history with the ghost stories passed down through generations – and you’ll come away knowing downtown Ephrata a little better, and maybe looking over your shoulder a little more. Harrisburg native Jeffrey Gaines, revered worldwide for his soul-searching lyrics and powerful live performances, brings his decades-spanning catalog to the stage. item.description:

Mike and Roberta will present the Dinosaur Adventure Show. They will explain how they became interested in science and the work of a scientist. The presentation will feature an Albertosaurs skull. They will highlight the features of this carnivore and examine the characteristics of this dinosaur. Audience members will experience the thrill of digging up a real Triceratops dinosaur bone and then help construct a dinosaur on a large cut-out. Audience participation, a touch of magic, and show & tell with rare fossils will round out this fun, educational, and exciting adventure!As an added attraction, Mike and Roberta will set-up a mini museum, showcasing photos and minerals from their summer digs in South Dakota. item.description: With Father David Peck and Professor Randall Zachman Entirely on Zoom Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. Join North Museum at Millport Conservancy on Thursday, October 29, from 7:00–9:00 PM for a FREE night of stargazing! Explore the night sky as we turn our telescopes toward dazzling stars, the magnificent rings of Saturn, and even Algol, the mysterious “Demon Star,” as it begins to dim during its celestial eclipse. item.title: Wee Build Free Play — Thu Jan 14, 2:00 PM — Manheim Township
item.description:
STEM, Toddlers, Children
Drop-in program. No registration required.Let your child’s imagination soar in this hands-on free play program! Designed for kids ages 2-7, this engaging session provides a creative and interactive environment where children can explore, build, and learn through play. No registration is required.Using vibrant magnetic tiles and a variety of manipulatives such as blocks, gears, and more, children will:Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills.Enhance fine motor abilities and hand-eye coordination.Foster collaboration and social interaction with peers.This open-ended program encourages creativity, exploration, and discovery, all while having fun! Whether constructing towering structures, creating intricate patterns, or experimenting with new ideas, kids will enjoy a safe, educational experience.Each family group must include a responsible adult in the room at all times. item.title: Know Thy Shelf! Teen Book Club — Thu Jan 14, 6:00 PM — Quarryville
item.description:
Book Club, Summer Reading, Teens
Ages 11-17. Snacks will be provided. Please register for each session you are able to attend. The goal of this club will be to develop lifelong reading habits, learn tips on getting the most out of your library, and accepting a genre challenge. Teens seeking leadership service hours may contact Sharon Roche for details. Please bring a book you are currently reading to each meeting. We will meet alternate Thursdays during the summer except where noted on the event calendar. Attendees can advocate for additions to our teen collection, program requests, and more!
Source: Lancaster Libraries

A monthly evening storytime (pajamas, your favorite stuffie and cozy blanket welcome) for birth to 6 years old. Come enjoy picture books and songs that will help us calm down for the evening and rest our minds. Please bring your own blanket or towel as we will be sitting on the floor together all warm and cozy.We thank Reynolds & Shivery, our Early Childhood program sponsors.
